UNDP official: 'Gaza's suffering must compel us to ask difficult questions'
A top United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) official has said the suffering endured by people in Gaza "must compel us to ask difficult questions".
“What strikes you immediately is the scale of the destruction in Gaza, where more than 90 per cent of the population depends on humanitarian assistance. The contrast between what we consider normal - food, water and quality of life - and the suffering endured by people in Gaza must compel us to ask difficult questions,” Haoliang Xu, under-secretary-general and associate administrator, UNDP, said.
Xu said a defining feature of our time is "polycrisis, with challenges that extend far beyond any one place", according to a post on X by MED Dialogues.
"The conflict in the Middle East, for example, is costing countries across the region at least 3.6 per cent of GDP, with some UNDP estimates reaching 6 per cent,” Xu said.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Israel has not acted on calls to protect Palestinian olive farmers, Ocha says
data.author: Hilal Saki
data.summary:
Israel has not acted on calls to protect Palestinian olive farmers, Ocha says
Calls on the Israeli authorities to protect Palestinian olive farmers and ensure they can reach their groves safely have not been acted upon, the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (Ocha) said, citing the Humanitarian Country Team.
Instead, in the first nine months of 2026, Israeli authorities uprooted or otherwise damaged more than 10,000 Palestinian-owned trees and saplings across the West Bank, mostly olives, the statement adds.
The Humanitarian Country Team for the Occupied Palestinian Territory, which brings together UN bodies and humanitarian NGOs, said more than 400 Israeli settler attacks on the Palestinian olive harvest since September have resulted in casualties or damage to property, including to more than 4,000 trees and saplings.
The number of attacks this year exceeds that recorded in any previous olive harvest season. This year’s harvesting window is closing, the team said, but there is still some time to act.
"Humanitarian NGOs and UN agencies urge the Israeli authorities in the strongest possible terms: end all attacks on Palestinians and their livelihoods, as required by international law. Ensure farmers have free, safe, sufficient and reliable access to their land. The team added that perpetrators must be stopped and held to account," the statement read.

data.author: Hilal Saki

Gaza Board of Peace says it will hand keys to UN if Israel fails to honour commitments
A senior adviser to the Donald Trump-appointed Gaza Peace Council has warned that the body could return responsibility for the enclave to the United Nations if Israel does not honour its commitments under the 20-point plan, Israeli outlet Ynet has reported.
Josh Gruenbaum, who was appointed to the council by Trump and previously worked in the White House, told Ynet: “We have been extremely patient and have given Israel its space. But it is frustrating that now, with the elections behind us - even if they haven’t resulted in a clear coalition - that Israel is failing to move forward on the commitments [Benjamin] Netanyahu made to President Trump.”
“If this political leadership says it no longer wants to honour what they committed to, just let us know,” Gruenbaum said, “and we will throw the keys back to the UN.”
Ynet said it had seen a presentation prepared by council members, who visited Israel last week. Its final slide, titled “Other alternatives to Gaza”, reportedly lists several scenarios if the plan is abandoned.
These include a future US administration and Congress ordering a different reconstruction plan, the UN Security Council taking over “perhaps through UNRWA”, the Palestinian Authority and Hamas.
The last scenario, according to the slide, is that Israel becomes fully responsible for the administrative and humanitarian costs of Gaza’s population.
Another slide reportedly says Hamas formally accepted the plan in July, pledging to give up its weapons and transfer governmental powers to the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza (NCAG), the technocratic body meant to run the territory.
“We are at a standstill due to political elements within the Netanyahu government who have prevented us from progressing and from testing whether Hamas will keep its word,” Gruenbaum said, according to Ynet.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Rights group calls for ban on white phosphorus, cites Israel's use in Gaza
data.author: Hilal Saki
data.summary:
Rights group calls for ban on white phosphorus, cites Israel's use in Gaza
Cairo-based rights group, Maat for Peace, Development and Human Rights, has called for an explicit ban on the use of white phosphorus, which has repeatedly been used by Israel in Gaza and southern Lebanon, Al Jazeera reported.
White phosphorus can cause severe burns, ignite repeatedly and produce intense heat and toxic smoke.
Human rights groups and The New York Times said in June that they had documented Israel's use of the chemical white phosphorus over civilian areas in Lebanon.
White phosphorus is not banned under international law, but it is illegal to use the chemical in and near populated areas since it can cause widespread harm. Israel has been accused by the international human rights community for decades of using the substance in a way that puts civilians in danger.
In a working paper submitted at the review session for the UN Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons, the group said the current treaty has glaring gaps that allow for the use of white phosphorus.
Following an impasse after talks started on Monday, the conference ran over time and ended early on Saturday, with states agreeing to continue talks aimed at developing measures on lethal autonomous weapons by 2028.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Pro-Palestine donor James Chambers released, says 'my sacrifice is very small'
data.author: Hilal Saki
data.summary:
Pro-Palestine donor James Chambers released, says 'my sacrifice is very small'
Spain's High Court has released pro-Palestinian donor and US media heir James Cox Chambers Jr on conditional bail, while it considers an extradition request by the US, according to a court ruling released on Friday.
The court said it had decided to release Chambers after US authorities acknowledged what they described as substantial and unintentional errors in the Spanish translation of an FBI agent's sworn statement submitted in support of the extradition request.
On his release, Chambers told Reuters he believed the accusations against him were baseless and politically motivated, adding that he had been alone in a cell for what "felt like a long time".
"I'm glad that this is a step in the right direction," he said.
Chambers added: "At the end of the day, I understand that most of the sacrifice I've had to make is very, very small in relation to the struggle that we are all a part of for the Palestinian people, for their liberation, for their sovereignty, for their respect, for the right to live."
"But in the context of just being alone in a cell all the time, it feels like a long time. I just missed my family. I really missed my family and my friends,” Chambers said.
Chambers, whose family owns Cox Enterprises, was arrested at the request of US authorities on 10 July while on holiday in Ibiza. He has been held in custody ever since on accusations including riot, conspiracy to commit riot and international money laundering. Chambers, known as Fergie, denies wrongdoing.
Separately, Chambers' lawyers said they were challenging a raid by Irish police on his family home in Dublin, which they said was conducted at the request of US authorities and involved the seizure of electronic devices and other property. His legal team said it would seek judicial review unless authorities clarify the legal basis for the operation.
Report by Reuters

data.author: Hilal Saki
data.summary:
Fire at Iraqi power station leaves four dead, 30 injured
At least four people were killed and 30 injured in a fire at a power station in southern Iraq on Saturday, with the toll expected to rise, security officials said.
Civil defence teams brought the fire at the Hartha power station north of Basra under control after firefighters responded to the incident, Iraq's state news agency, INA, reported.
The fire spread to neighbouring houses and forced operations at the power station to stop, the security officials said.
The Hartha station has an installed generating capacity of 800 megawatts but had been operating at around 400 megawatts before the fire, they said.
There was no immediate official information on the cause of the fire or the extent of the damage, INA reported.

data.title: Middle East Eye: UK, France and China vote against UAE's Lana Nusseibeh at UN
data.author: Oscar Rickett
data.summary:
UK, France and China vote against UAE's Lana Nusseibeh at UN
Lana Nusseibeh's bid to become the next secretary-general of the United Nations suffered a setback on Friday after the UK, France and China all voted against the Emirati diplomat in the latest informal straw poll conducted to help determine who should replace Antonio Guterres.
Along with the US and Russia, the countries make up three of the P5, the permanent members of the UN Security Council that can veto any prospective candidate for the world body's top job.
While votes in the straw poll are cast anonymously, diplomatic and other sources close to the Security Council told Middle East Eye that the UK, China and France were the P5 members who had voted to "discourage" Nusseibeh's candidacy.
The US, Russia and Israel - which is not currently part of the Security Council and thus does not vote - all back Nusseibeh, according to the same sources.
In total, the UAE minister of state and former ambassador to the UN received seven "encourage" votes, six "discourage" votes and two "no opinion" votes - the same result she achieved in the last straw poll, held on 6 November.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Explosive-laden boxes dropped from the sky: Israel’s latest weapon in Gaza
data.author: Daniel Tester
data.summary:
Explosive-laden boxes dropped from the sky: Israel’s latest weapon in Gaza
Jaber Yaseen's family was preparing the traditional maftoul dish for their Friday family lunch when they heard a loud engine approaching.
The Palestinian family of 13 were startled by the noise, which grew louder as it approached their home in the al-Zaytoon neighbourhood, east of Gaza City.
“I thought it was an Israeli tank at first. I looked out of the window and was shocked to see a huge quadcopter drone carrying two boxes of explosives, flying low over our neighbourhood,” Yaseen told Middle East Eye.
“I watched the drone move towards us. Without any warning, it dropped the two boxes of explosives onto our roof. I was terrified for my children's lives. I grabbed them and rushed out of the house, knowing the explosives could detonate at any moment. We couldn't take anything with us.”
Panic spread as families watched more Israeli drones dropping explosives onto rooftops across the neighbourhood. Dozens were forced to flee their homes, with nowhere to go.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Iran says new air defence system intercepted US Reaper drone over Hormuz
data.author: MEE staff
data.summary:
Iran says new air defence system intercepted US Reaper drone over Hormuz
Submitted by
MEE staff
on
Sat, 11/21/2026 - 09:50
The US reported losing at least 45 Reaper drones by August, while Iran says its forces have now destroyed 58 since the war began
A crew member monitors an MQ-9 Reaper military drone at Cognac air base in Chateaubernard, southwestern France, 12 June 2026 (Christophe Archambault/AFP)
Off
The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said it shot down a US MQ-9 Reaper drone in the Strait of Hormuz, Iranian state media reported on Saturday.
The IRGC said it is the 58th aircraft destroyed by Iranian forces since the start of the war, adding that the drone was detected, tracked and destroyed by Iran’s new air defence system.
In August, the US military said that it had lost at least 45 MQ-9 Reaper drones during the war, amounting to roughly a quarter of its fleet, according to three US officials cited by The Washington Post.
The newspaper estimated the losses could represent more than $1.3bn in equipment costs.
The development comes amid renewed tensions between Washington and Tehran, with attacks on commercial vessels near the Strait of Hormuz.
A commercial tanker was hit by an unknown missile about 11 nautical miles north of Khasab port in Oman, in the Strait of Hormuz, the UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) said.
The US military said on Tuesday that it had attacked a missile launching site on Iran’s Qeshm Island in retaliation for attacks by Iran on US personnel and property.
Iran later said it had attacked US drone and missile facilities at the Ali al-Salem air base in Kuwait.

Kuwait reported responding to "hostile drone activity", while Bahrain said it had intercepted Iranian aerial attacks.

data.summary:
Fresh Israeli attack on Gaza kills three
Three Palestinians were killed by an Israeli airstrike on a vehicle in Gaza City's Tel-al Hawa neighbourhood on Saturday.
The attack, which was reported by the Wafa news agency and corroborated by Al Jazeera reporters based in the enclave, also injured several people.
Over 1,600 Palestinians have been killed by ongoing Israeli attacks since the October 2025 ceasefire agreement between Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's government and Hamas, with the total Palestinian death toll in the enclave since October 2023 exceeding 74,000.

data.author: Daniel Tester
data.summary:
Iran says it downed US drone over Qeshm Island
Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps has said that it has destroyed a US Predator drone over Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz.
The US claimed that its fighter jets used "precision munitions” to strike an Iranian missile site on the island last Tuesday.
Qeshm is the largest island in the Gulf and is seen as strategically significant, given its position at the gateway of Hormuz.
